_about: Read Oasis pronunciation lexicon. Source of truth for how a word should sound; TTS is only the renderer. IPA follows the conventions used by Oxford Learner's / Cambridge dictionaries (RP-style UK, General American US) but every transcription here was written by the maintainer; no dictionary text, data files or audio were copied. '.' marks syllable breaks, 'ˈ' primary and 'ˌ' secondary stress. 'stress' is the 1-based index of the primary-stressed syllable. Rows marked review:true still need a parent/teacher check against a dictionary before being trusted.

apple.definition: A round fruit, red or green, that grows on a tree.
apple.example: I eat an apple every day.

banana.notes: UK ɑː vs US æ in the stressed syllable

water.notes: UK non-rhotic; US flapped t and r-coloured vowel

school.definition: The place where children go to learn.
school.example: I go to school every day.

teacher.definition: A person who helps you learn.
teacher.example: My teacher reads us a story.

three.notes: voiceless th; hard for Vietnamese speakers (often t or s)

think.definition: To use your mind; to have an idea.

this.notes: voiced th; often d or z for Vietnamese speakers

that.definition: The thing there, away from me.

world.definition: The Earth and everything on it.
world.example: There are many countries in the world.
world.notes: dark l after a long vowel; -rld cluster is hard

girl.example: The girl has a red kite.

bird.definition: An animal with feathers and wings.
bird.example: A bird sings in the tree.

computer.definition: A machine you use for work, games and the internet.

because.example: I am wet because it rained.
because.notes: UK ɒ vs US ʌ; weak form bɪkəz in fast speech

schedule.definition: A plan of when things will happen.
schedule.example: The bus schedule is on the wall.
schedule.notes: Classic UK/US split: ʃ vs sk. Many TTS voices default to the US form even in en-GB; pin with IPA.

garage.definition: A building where a car is kept.
garage.example: The car is in the garage.
garage.notes: UK stress on 1st syllable (also ˈɡær.ɪdʒ); US on 2nd

tomato.definition: A soft red fruit used in salads and sauces.
tomato.example: I put a tomato in my sandwich.

advertisement.definition: A picture, film or words that try to make you buy something.
advertisement.example: There is an advertisement for juice on TV.
advertisement.notes: UK stress 2nd syllable, US 3rd with aɪ

vitamin.definition: Something in food that keeps your body healthy.
vitamin.notes: UK ɪ vs US aɪ in the first syllable

very.notes: v vs Vietnamese j/z; keep lips-teeth contact

vegetable.definition: A plant you eat, like a carrot or a bean.

comfortable.definition: Nice to sit, lie or be in; not hurting.
comfortable.notes: three syllables; the 'or' is not pronounced as spelt

kite.definition: A light toy you fly in the wind on a string.
kite.example: The kite went up in the wind.

seed.definition: The small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.

swells.definition: Gets bigger, like a sponge full of water.
swells.example: The balloon swells as you blow into it.

root.definition: The part of a plant that grows down into the soil.
root.example: The root drinks water from the ground.

sprout.definition: A new, young plant shoot that has just started to grow.
sprout.example: A sprout came up in the pot.

slips.definition: Slides down or away by itself.
slips.example: The soap slips out of my hand.

then.example: I put on my shoes. Then I go out.

hatches.example: The turtle hatches on the beach.

led.definition: Went in a line toward a place.
led.example: The path led to the gate.

tail.definition: The long strip hanging from a kite.

heavy.definition: Hard to lift; weighs a lot.
heavy.example: The bag of rice is heavy.

puddle.definition: A small pool of rain water on the ground.

soaks.definition: Goes slowly into something, like water into a sponge.
soaks.example: The rain soaks into my socks.

vapor.definition: Water that has turned into a gas.
vapor.notes: UK spelling is 'vapour'; book text uses 'vapor' for simplicity

evaporation.definition: When water turns into vapor and goes into the air.
evaporation.example: Wet clothes dry because of evaporation.

list.definition: Words written one under another so you remember them.

stall.definition: A small open shop at a market.

yuki.notes: Pinned so no voice says 'yucky' or 'yoo-kai'.

football.definition: A game where two teams kick a ball into a goal.

friends.definition: People you like and know well.

reading.definition: Looking at words and understanding them.
